summary: First full test pass on ASCENDENCY. Backend (pytest, 15 tests) 100% passing across auth, simulations, profile, leaderboard. Frontend end-to-end flow verified: register → auto-login → logout → re-login → simulation (mode-30 → countdown → typing arena captures keys → live metrics update → HeroReveal appears with hero classification VANGUARD) → persistence in /profile and /leaderboard (with '◆ YOU' marker) → sort buttons work → hero-card open/close overlay → brand-logo navigates home. No console/page errors during authenticated flow (initial 401s from /api/auth/me before login are expected). Gold eyebrow labels 'ASCENDENCY ◆ PERFORMANCE PROTOCOL', 'SYSTEM MODULES', 'THE ASCENDANCY ◆ HERO ARCHIVE' render in bright gold rgb(245,197,66). Animated tactical borders (brd-top/bottom/left/right) present on home-begin-btn, home-ascendancy-btn, and all four module cards (MOD-01..MOD-04).

ui_bugs.component: Home.jsx line 87 – NEURAL LINK ◆ STABLE / LATENCY 004ms readout
ui_bugs.issue: Uses class 'text-gold-bright/70' (70% opacity). The bug-fix requirement states this readout should render in bright gold and be visible (not dim/washed out). At 70% opacity on the dark navy background it still appears slightly muted compared to the fully-bright ASCENDENCY / SYSTEM MODULES eyebrows. Consider removing '/70' to make it fully bright, or bumping to '/90'.

action_items: (Optional / low-priority) Brighten the 'NEURAL LINK ◆ STABLE' + 'LATENCY 004ms' readout on Home.jsx line 87 by removing the '/70' opacity modifier so it matches the other bright-gold eyebrow labels called out in the review request.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py – login route lacks brute-force lockout / rate-limiting despite playbook mentioning it. If lockout is a product requirement, add a per-email fail counter (auth playbook: lock after 5 failed attempts).

server.py cookie flags use secure=True + samesite='none' which is correct for cross-origin preview, but there is no CSRF protection for state-changing endpoints when cookies are used. Consider a CSRF token or SameSite=lax for same-site prod deployments.
server.py /api/leaderboard uses request as a default kwarg — works but relies on FastAPI DI order. Prefer explicit Depends or Optional[Request] with type hint for clarity.
server.py public_user returns average fields computed inline; consider caching or precomputing on write to avoid arithmetic on hot GETs.
Simulator.jsx – window-level keydown listener captures all keystrokes while phase==='running'; this could intercept typing when a modal opens mid-run. Not observed today, just a note.

No idempotency / anti-cheat validation on POST /api/simulations — client can submit arbitrary WPM up to server clamp of 400. Consider server-side reasonableness checks against duration & totalCharacters.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of critical flows (auth register/login/logout, simulation run, persistence, leaderboard, ascendancy, navigation)

test_credentials: Admin: admin@ascendency.io / Ascend@2026. Test users are created dynamically each run with prefix TEST_ or testui_ and UI-generated random uid.
